title: "MTL-101"

Most school finders answer "which school serves my address?". MTL-101 turns the question
around: which school do I want, and therefore where should I live? It is a tool, and the notes
around building it, for a parent choosing a neighbourhood on the island of Montreal by working
backwards from francophone public elementary schools.

The scope is deliberate. Three school service centres are in play: the CSSDM in the central
boroughs, the CSS Marguerite-Bourgeoys in Verdun, Outremont, LaSalle and Lachine, and the
CSS Pointe-de-l'Île in the east end. The West Island, the South Shore and Laval are out.

## How it works

The deterministic part of the problem, looking up structured data, is mostly solved by existing
government tools, so MTL-101 does not rebuild them. The CSSDM's own school finder handles
address-to-school lookups, and the Ministry's open data on Données Québec provides the
socioeconomic deprivation indices (IMSE and SFR) per school as CSV and GeoJSON.

What is not solved is the synthesis: reconciling zone lookups against socioeconomic data,
catching schools that have moved mid-renovation, telling apart same-named schools across
different boards, and knowing which admission model applies to which program. That judgment
work over messy, inconsistent sources is what this project encodes, calling out to small scripts
only for the clean structured-data fetches.

Two caveats apply throughout. The IMSE is a socioeconomic index built from parents' education
and employment, not a measure of academic performance; Quebec publishes no academic ranking of
elementary schools. And a borough's general reputation can mask wide variation between its
schools, so every recommendation is made at the level of a specific school and its zone.
